prompt:
You are a senior information designer and editorial typographer who sets data tables for high-quality publications (statistical yearbooks, reference works, financial reports, technical documentation) in many writing systems, including Chinese. You judge by looking at the real rendered result.

Judge a table layout on all of these levels, in this order of necessity but as one whole:
1. correctness — every character visible, structure intact, nothing clipped or overlapping;
2. readability — natural line breaks, words/numbers/identifiers/semantic units kept whole, continuous reading;
3. function — easy to look up, compare, locate and understand the information for this table's real reading tasks;
4. visual order — alignment, grouping, hierarchy, consistent scale for elements with the same role;
5. visual rhythm — proportion, density changes, distribution of white space, spatial relationships;
6. overall aesthetics — balance, restraint, naturalness, harmony.
Do not assume that equal widths, symmetry, minimum height, the fewest lines, the golden ratio or any fixed proportion is good in itself; decide from this table's function, content and reading task, and look for counter-examples to your own rules.

Table: Customer Onboarding Field Validation Rules (language en).
Grid: 4 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes.
Measured content facts (text px at 15px font, padding excluded):
  col 1: header "Field" · longest unbreakable unit 126px · widest one-line content 126px
  col 2: header "Pattern" · longest unbreakable unit 114px · widest one-line content 1074px
  col 3: header "Example valid" · longest unbreakable unit 167px · widest one-line content 264px
  col 4: header "Error message" · longest unbreakable unit 157px · widest one-line content 700px
Each column adds 21px of padding+border to its text width.
Viewport: 360px wide (dashed pink box in the renders). At 360px some words cannot fit unsplit. Horizontal scrolling is ALLOWED: the table may be wider than 360px (column widths summing to more than 359px) (the reader scrolls), or you may fit within 359px and accept the consequences. Fitting and scrolling layouts are judged as two separate classes; propose good layouts of BOTH kinds.
Rendering convention: a full render shows the WHOLE table; anything right of the dashed box is not clipped — it is reached by scrolling. Where a layout scrolls, an extra "viewport view" image shows only what is visible at first sight.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. Only the column widths are designed; row heights follow from them.

Your understanding: {"purpose":"Document validation rules for customer onboarding fields, pairing each field's pattern with a valid example and a corrective error message.","tasks":["Find a field and inspect its validation rule.","Compare a pattern with its valid example.","Read the error message to understand how to correct an invalid value."],"relations":["Each row links one field to its regular expression, example and error message.","Examples illustrate the patterns; error messages explain the requirements in reader-facing language."],"roles":["Field names are row headers and lookup keys.","Pattern contains technical validation expressions.","Example valid supplies concrete test values.","Error message provides correction guidance."],"keep_whole":["Field identifiers, example values and meaningful regex tokens should stay intact wherever space permits.","Digits, punctuation and character order in patterns and examples must remain legible."],"may_wrap":["Error messages can wrap at natural word boundaries.","Long regular expressions may wrap, though breaks make them harder to inspect.","In a viewport-fitting table, long identifiers and examples may need to split."],"same_scale":["Field names and examples benefit from compact but sufficient widths for their identifiers.","Pattern and error message columns need more space, with their relative widths determined by whether code inspection or prose reading is the priority."],"h_vs_v":"A fitting table avoids horizontal scrolling but forces severe breaks and tall rows. Scrolling buys legible identifiers, examples and prose; additional pattern width can greatly reduce the height of the long email rule, at the cost of more horizontal travel."}

Image 1 is the one-line content overview. Then real browser renders of: d2r1A (full view, then viewport view), d2r1B, d2r0B (full view, then viewport view).
Measured facts:
d2r1A: column widths [147, 390, 285, 300] px · table 1123×547 px · row heights [36, 83, 83, 60, 60, 83, 83, 60] · column headers on >1 line: 0/4 · tallest cell 3 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · WIDER than the viewport by 763 px (horizontal scrolling)
d2r1B: column widths [95, 90, 78, 96] px · table 360×2035 px · row heights [60, 525, 292, 199, 176, 292, 269, 222] · column headers on >1 line: 2/4 · tallest cell 22 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 21 · fits the 360 px viewport (no scrolling)
d2r0B: column widths [147, 260, 285, 300] px · table 993×593 px · row heights [36, 129, 83, 60, 60, 83, 83, 60] · column headers on >1 line: 0/4 · tallest cell 5 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · WIDER than the viewport by 633 px (horizontal scrolling)

Look at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design: what works, what is visually wrong, and the cause (which width). Then either propose up to 3 improved designs (refine the most promising, fix what you saw, or try an important unexplored idea) or, if further changes would not bring a meaningful improvement, set "done": true. Do not resubmit near-identical widths.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"best":["your best design name(s) so far"],"done":false,"designs":[{"widths":[int px],"change":"what and why"}]}
